summary.intent: Implement the pending todo `2026-07-01-ci-tee-worker-for-tee-republish-e2e.md`: wire a real TEE worker into CI so the sdk-e2e `tee-republish` test can run live instead of being skipped, then commit and push the result.
summary.outcome: Fully implemented and verified: ci.yml now builds and starts the tee-worker headless in simulator mode before the API boots, wires matching TEE_WORKER_URL/SECRET and DB/redis env into the sdk-e2e job, the test's SKIP_TEE_LIVE gate was removed, the todo was moved to completed with a resolution note, and a live smoke test plus a 10-point adversarial diff review both passed. Changes were staged and committed (signed) on `feat/tee-lease-renewer-contract-rewrite`; push was in progress at transcript end.

repo: tee_key_state.current_public_key is populated by a one-shot NestJS OnModuleInit hook (TeeModule.onModuleInit -> TeeService.initializeFromTee), not a cron or endpoint — it runs unconditionally regardless of NODE_ENV.

All errors in the TEE bootstrap are swallowed twice (tee.service.ts and tee.module.ts), so if the worker is unreachable/unauthenticated at API boot, tee_key_state silently stays empty instead of failing loudly.
TEE_WORKER_SECRET must be non-empty and match between API and worker or /public-key 401s (worker authMiddleware) and bootstrap silently no-ops.
Code default TEE_WORKER_URL port is 3001 (mock), but the real local/CI simulator worker runs on 3002 — must explicitly set TEE_WORKER_URL=http://localhost:3002.
No TEE_REPUBLISH_ENABLED or TEE_EPOCH_* feature flags exist anywhere in apps/api/src; republish cron and key-state bootstrap always run.
apps/api migrationsRun: true (app.module.ts:104) means migrations auto-apply on API boot — no separate CI migration step needed for schema changes like ScheduleCollapse.
tee-worker simulator mode derives keys via HKDF from a fixed seed — no dstack socket, DB, or redis required; it only refuses to start if CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT (or NODE_ENV) is 'production'.
ci.yml's `changes` path filter routes both `.github/**` and `tests/**` to the sdk-e2e job's trigger set.

tee-republish.test.ts is the only sdk-e2e suite touching DB/redis directly, so scoping DB_DATABASE/REDIS_PORT env only to that step doesn't affect other suites; suites also run sequentially (fileParallelism:false).
Completed todos in this repo are moved from .planning/todos/pending/ to completed/ with a brief resolution note appended, sometimes with a `resolves_phase` marker.

code.finding: OnModuleInit calls teeService.initializeFromTee(); errors are caught here and again inside the service, so failures never surface.
TEE_WORKER_URL defaults to http://localhost:3001 and TEE_WORKER_SECRET defaults to '' — empty secret means no Authorization header is sent (lines 212-218).
Worker returns 500 if TEE_WORKER_SECRET is unset server-side, 401 on mismatch; uses timingSafeEqual for comparison.
Simulator mode is rejected only when CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT==='production' (or unset NODE_ENV==='production') — safe for CI with CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT=development.
Republish cron is a BullMQ upsertJobScheduler on '0 */6 * * *' — does not populate tee_key_state and never fires once at startup.

workflow: A background Workflow with parallel readers can partially misfire — one reader returned placeholder junk ('test', 'file:1') while others returned thorough evidence-backed findings; always sanity-check structured workflow output before trusting it, and fall back to direct file reads for the failed portion rather than re-running the whole workflow.
Truncated task-notification results should be read in full from the output file before deciding a section is unusable.

Running a live smoke test of the riskiest assumption (headless worker startup) after implementation, in addition to static lint/type/YAML checks, caught a real environment collision (a pre-existing worker already bound to port 3002) that would have been invisible otherwise.

Dispatching an adversarial-review subagent against the full diff with an explicit numbered checklist (ordering, secret/port match, redis, DB, dangling refs, build, env precedence, collateral damage, simulator gating) produced high-confidence, file:line-cited confirmation before declaring the task done.
